Lat was also pretty great, minor lane hugging but only on narrow roads.

Long was very smooth, no mistakes made

Lat - 9/10
Long - Not Tested (I'm a scaredy cat)

Its better at right turns than left turns, though I'm not sure if that's just my car or not. It definitely has a right bias, but Its not as bad as other models. (YMMV)
Right turns felt effortless for it, more "aggressive", "confident", however you want to put it. It didn't seem to care too much about crossing the right line when making sharper right curves, but I've been told that's normal across other models.
There were a couple times I took a right curve and it hugged the right line a little more than I'd like, but I like to be in the middle of the lane at all times, so it might be very comfortable for you.
Left turns felt more "cautious" or afraid of crossing the left lane line while going through a left curve. I'll take it since that's more likely to avoid an accident.
It does feel like there is oscillation at times, but It's not consistent. I wonder if that's just what happens when a model is allowed to be more aggressive with corrections.
It did perfectly on a tight S-curve in my city, so its an A in my book. The only think that could have made it better is if it was more smooth at minor corrections like DTR3.

TLDR: Pretty good overall, but has the tendency to hug right at times.

Personally, I prefer the TR13 model. It's on par with the TR10, and both perform better than the TR7 in my opinion.😆
Confirmed with hkg-angle something is seriously wrong with TR13. It can't stay in lane. It is constantly crossing the left or right line. TR7 is way better at keeping in lane for some reason.

Used this one on the way to work this morning. Lateral was great smooth curves and even did intersections well. Long could be better though I got the big brake alert and had to step in to stop the car and I feel like it gets close to the lead car and then stops hard instead of smoothing into it.
Here is an example of what I was talking about not getting alerts. In this instance it just gave up.
This happened to me before. It’s usually fixed when you turn off nnlc. Sometimes it’s fixed for me by restarting or updating the device
This was with NNLC off. I tended to blamle that setting in the past, but it seems like this happened to me on a lot of the TR series models.
I see. I feel like there could be a mismatch between the actual torque in the CX5 and what the model thinks it has. This happened to me on older models as well.
FWIW this kind of thing happens a lot less often in my car when NNLC is *on*.   The MLSIM models do better too, like SP Vikander and generally TR.

My theory is when it "gives up" like this, it's when where the model wants to go and the car was able to steer - though not saturating, diverge enough that the lateral control loop temporarily "breaks."   Help it through the curve/turn and it re-engages when they're again closer.
exactly my experience

TR13 is the best lateral model that I have tested and used with my Ioniq 6 HDA2 so far. 
Tight curves are taken cleanly at the appropriate speed. Wide bends are handled very well, even at higher speeds.
It still happens that the steering wheel is jerkily straightened at some corner exits, but it is much rarer than before. 
Yesterday, however, at a set of traffic lights, my car wanted to follow the car in front, which had turned right. But I wanted to drive straight ahead. I had to intervene intensively. 
But I think the model is developing in the right direction.
